benzodiazepines.sentence: MedlinePlus says diazepam is used to relieve anxiety, to control agitation caused by alcohol withdrawal, to control muscle spasms and stiffness caused by certain nerve disorders and to control seizures.
benzodiazepines.note: MedlinePlus Diazepam excerpt: 'used to relieve anxiety, control agitation caused by alcohol withdrawal, control muscle spasms and stiffness caused by certain nerve disorders, and to control seizures'

benzodiazepines.sentence: The NHS describes diazepam as generally for short-term use, because longer use can cause addiction and withdrawal symptoms.
benzodiazepines.note: Search summary of NHS diazepam page said use is generally short term because longer use can cause addiction and withdrawal; blended with trust leaflets, so page attribution uncertain

benzodiazepines.sentence: MedlinePlus says diazepam, as a benzodiazepine, works by calming abnormal overactivity in the brain.
benzodiazepines.note: 'It works by calming abnormal overactivity in the brain.'

benzodiazepines.sentence: A review in the NIH's PubMed Central archive says benzodiazepines act mainly on the GABA-A receptor and produce sedative effects.
benzodiazepines.note: PMC review excerpt: 'BZDs primarily work on the GABA-A receptor subunit'; sedative effects stated in same summary

benzodiazepines.sentence: NHS inform says tolerance can develop quickly with frequent use.
benzodiazepines.note: NHS inform dependence section: tolerance can build quickly with frequent use

benzodiazepines.sentence: The same review says regular use can cause physical and psychological dependence, with withdrawal symptoms similar to alcohol withdrawal, some of which can be life-threatening.
benzodiazepines.note: PMC review excerpt on dependence and withdrawal resembling alcohol withdrawal; some life-threatening

benzodiazepines.sentence: The NHS lists feeling drowsy, tired or less alert among the common side effects of diazepam.
benzodiazepines.note: NHS diazepam side effects list as returned in summary: less alert, drowsy, tiredness, low blood pressure

benzodiazepines.sentence: Serious side effects of diazepam are uncommon; the NHS lists allergic reactions, slow or shallow breathing and yellowing of the skin or eyes.
benzodiazepines.note: NHS serious side effects as returned in summary

benzodiazepines.sentence: NHS inform says benzodiazepines mixed with other depressants such as alcohol, gabapentin and opioids can pose serious health risks, and advises against taking other drugs or more benzodiazepines to deal with withdrawal symptoms.
benzodiazepines.note: NHS inform: mixing with alcohol, gabapentin, opioids poses serious risk; avoid other drugs or more benzodiazepines for withdrawal

benzodiazepines.sentence: NHS inform says a gradual reduction can greatly ease unpleasant withdrawal symptoms.
benzodiazepines.note: NHS inform withdrawal section: gradual reduction can greatly ease unpleasant symptoms

benzodiazepines.sentence: In an emergency, such as a suspected overdose or severe withdrawal, call 999; NHS 111 or the GP can advise urgently; Samaritans on 116 123 is free at any time.
benzodiazepines.note: Site signposting rule (README: crisis route wherever overdose or severe withdrawal is mentioned), not a retrieved claim

z-drugs.sentence: The NHS describes zopiclone as a prescription-only sleeping medicine for short-term treatment of severe insomnia.
z-drugs.note: NHS zopiclone page: sleeping pill that can be taken for short-term treatment of severe insomnia; prescription-only per search summary

z-drugs.sentence: MedlinePlus warns that zolpidem can cause serious, possibly life-threatening sleep behaviours, such as driving, preparing and eating food or making phone calls while not fully awake, without remembering it afterwards.
z-drugs.note: MedlinePlus Zolpidem warning as returned: driven, prepared and eaten food, had sex, made phone calls while not fully awake, no memory

z-drugs.sentence: A StatPearls review says zolpidem binds preferentially to one benzodiazepine receptor subtype, whereas benzodiazepines act on all subtypes.
z-drugs.note: StatPearls NBK442008 as summarised: binds preferentially to BZ1 subtype, unlike benzodiazepines which act on all subtypes; source text fragmentary

z-drugs.sentence: NICE says that, as with benzodiazepines, the sedative effects of the Z-drugs may persist into the next day.
z-drugs.note: TA77 document excerpt: 'In common with the benzodiazepines, the sedative effects of the Z-drugs may persist the next day.'

z-drugs.sentence: The NHS lists a dry mouth, a bitter or metallic taste, and feeling tired, sleepy, dazed or less alert the next day as common side effects of zopiclone.
z-drugs.note: NHS zopiclone common side effects as returned in summary

z-drugs.sentence: The NHS lists sleepwalking, or doing things while not fully awake, along with allergic reactions and mental health problems, as serious side effects of zopiclone.
z-drugs.note: NHS zopiclone serious side effects as returned in summary

z-drugs.sentence: The NHS says zopiclone may not be suitable for people with sleep apnoea or other breathing problems, liver problems, muscle weakness, or a history of alcohol, drug or opioid addiction.

The NHS says it is possible to become addicted to zopiclone, and that stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms such as feeling agitated or anxious, so a doctor usually reduces the dose gradually.
z-drugs.note: NHS zopiclone page: possible to become addicted; do not stop suddenly; withdrawal agitation or anxiety; gradual reduction

z-drugs.sentence: NICE notes that the risk of dependence and withdrawal should be considered when prescribing Z-drugs, and that rebound insomnia can occur on stopping.
z-drugs.note: TA77 excerpts: 'As with all benzodiazepines, the risk of dependence and withdrawal syndrome should be considered'; 'Rebound insomnia also occurs'

z-drugs.sentence: In an emergency, such as a suspected overdose or severe withdrawal, call 999; NHS 111 or the GP can advise urgently; Samaritans on 116 123 is free at any time.
z-drugs.note: Site signposting rule, not a retrieved claim

nitroimidazoles.sentence: The NHS says metronidazole is an antibiotic used for bacterial infections, including skin infections, mouth infections, bacterial vaginosis and pelvic inflammatory disease, and is available only on prescription.
nitroimidazoles.note: NHS About metronidazole as returned in summary

nitroimidazoles.sentence: MedlinePlus says tinidazole treats trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis, giardiasis and amoebiasis, and describes it as a nitroimidazole antimicrobial.
nitroimidazoles.note: MedlinePlus Tinidazole: treats trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis, giardiasis, amebiasis; class nitroimidazole antimicrobials

nitroimidazoles.sentence: A pharmacology review says metronidazole acts against various protozoa and most anaerobic bacteria, but not against aerobic microorganisms.
nitroimidazoles.note: PubMed 363399/9360057 excerpts: limited spectrum encompassing various protozoans and most Gram-negative and Gram-positive anaerobes; lacks efficacy against aerobic organisms

nitroimidazoles.sentence: A review of tinidazole describes it as active in the laboratory against most clinically important anaerobic bacteria.
nitroimidazoles.note: PubMed 6749473: 'active in vitro against most clinically important obligate anaerobes'

nitroimidazoles.sentence: The NHS lists feeling or being sick, diarrhoea and a slight metallic taste in the mouth as common side effects of metronidazole.
nitroimidazoles.note: NHS side effects of metronidazole as returned

nitroimidazoles.sentence: MedlinePlus lists a sharp, unpleasant metallic taste, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite among the effects of tinidazole.
nitroimidazoles.note: MedlinePlus Tinidazole side effects as returned

nitroimidazoles.sentence: The NHS lists yellowing of the whites of the eyes or skin as a sign of liver or gallbladder problems that needs medical contact.
nitroimidazoles.note: NHS side effects page as returned; route to care (GP/NHS 111) not stated in the returned text

nitroimidazoles.sentence: MedlinePlus advises avoiding alcohol and products containing alcohol during tinidazole treatment and for a period afterwards, as they may cause an upset stomach, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating and flushing.
nitroimidazoles.note: MedlinePlus Tinidazole alcohol precaution (a number of days given; omitted here)

nitroimidazoles.sentence: A review notes that tinidazole labelling advises avoiding alcohol because of its chemical similarity to metronidazole, though the review found no data to support the concern.
nitroimidazoles.note: PMC7038249 excerpt: labelling recommends avoiding alcohol due to chemical similarity but data to support were not identified

nitroimidazoles.sentence: MedlinePlus advises telling the doctor about kidney or liver disease before using metronidazole.
nitroimidazoles.note: MedlinePlus Metronidazole as returned in summary

alpha-blockers.sentence: The NHS describes doxazosin as an alpha blocker used to lower high blood pressure, which can reduce the risk of a heart attack or stroke, and to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate such as problems with peeing.

A StatPearls review lists doxazosin, prazosin and terazosin as selective alpha-1 blockers used for high blood pressure, and describes them as second-line choices because of low blood pressure on standing.
alpha-blockers.note: StatPearls Alpha-Blockers NBK556066: second-line due to adverse effects, particularly orthostatic hypotension

alpha-blockers.sentence: The NHS says alpha blockers lower blood pressure by relaxing the blood vessels so that blood passes through more easily.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS: 'Alpha blockers reduce blood pressure by relaxing your blood vessels so blood can pass through them more easily.'

alpha-blockers.sentence: A StatPearls review explains that they act on the sympathetic nervous system, with selective alpha-1 blockers relaxing blood vessels by stopping noradrenaline from activating alpha-1 receptors.
alpha-blockers.note: StatPearls: modulate sympathetic nervous system; selective alpha-1 antagonists relax vessels by blocking norepinephrine at alpha-1 receptors

alpha-blockers.sentence: The same review says non-selective agents also block alpha-2 receptors, which can increase noradrenaline release and partly offset the widening of blood vessels.
alpha-blockers.note: StatPearls: nonselective agents also block alpha-2, can increase norepinephrine release and partly offset vasodilation

alpha-blockers.sentence: For doxazosin the NHS lists headaches, swollen feet, ankles or fingers, needing to pee suddenly or more often, and lower stomach pain as the main side effects, which are usually mild and short-lived.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS side effects of doxazosin as returned

alpha-blockers.sentence: For tamsulosin the NHS lists dizziness and problems with ejaculation, such as little or no semen, as the main side effects.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS Common questions about tamsulosin: main side effects dizzy and problems ejaculating

alpha-blockers.sentence: The NHS says dizziness is most likely when starting an alpha blocker, and that alcohol can make it worse, so it advises avoiding alcohol at first.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS tamsulosin and doxazosin pages as returned: dizzy when first starting; alcohol can worsen

alpha-blockers.sentence: MedlinePlus says dizziness on standing up quickly is more common with doxazosin when treatment starts, when the dose is increased, or when treatment has been stopped for a few days.
alpha-blockers.note: MedlinePlus Doxazosin as returned in summary

alpha-blockers.sentence: The NHS says to tell the doctor in advance about cataract or glaucoma surgery, because tamsulosin may cause complications during the operation.
The NHS says to tell a doctor or pharmacist about medicines for erectile dysfunction, such as sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil, when taking tamsulosin.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS Common questions about tamsulosin interactions

alpha-blockers.sentence: The NHS says to call NHS 111 after taking more than the prescribed amount of tamsulosin or doxazosin.
alpha-blockers.note: NHS tamsulosin and doxazosin pages: call 111 if taken more than prescribed

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: MedlinePlus says dutasteride is used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia, an enlarged prostate gland, and belongs to the 5-alpha reductase inhibitors.
The NHS says finasteride for hair loss is available only on a private prescription, not on the NHS.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: NHS About finasteride as returned in summary

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: A StatPearls review says dutasteride blocks all three forms of the 5-alpha reductase enzyme and lowers blood DHT more than finasteride does.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: StatPearls Dutasteride: inhibits all 3 isoenzymes; reduced serum DHT; comparison with finasteride from PMC review summary (finasteride lowers DHT less)

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: A systematic review found insufficient evidence that either finasteride or dutasteride has an advantage over the other in efficacy or safety for clinically important outcomes.

MedlinePlus lists difficulty getting or keeping an erection, reduced sex drive and ejaculation problems among the effects of dutasteride, and says breast changes such as lumps, pain or nipple discharge need prompt medical attention (US source).
StatPearls notes that sexual side effects may persist after dutasteride is stopped.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: StatPearls Dutasteride: sexual side effects may persist after discontinuation

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: The NHS says most men aged 18 or over can take finasteride, but it is generally not recommended for women or children.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: NHS Who can and cannot take finasteride as returned

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: The NHS lists depression or thoughts of self-harm, severe bladder problems and liver problems among the things to mention to the doctor before starting finasteride.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: NHS who can and cannot take finasteride as returned

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: The NHS says it is very unlikely that a partner taking finasteride will harm a woman or her baby.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: NHS Fertility and pregnancy while taking finasteride as returned

5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.sentence: MedlinePlus says women who are or may become pregnant should not handle dutasteride capsules, and that blood should not be donated during treatment and for a period afterwards (US source).
Anyone with low mood or thoughts of self-harm can call NHS 111 and choose the mental health option, or Samaritans on 116 123, free at any time; 999 for immediate danger.
5-alpha-reductase-inhibitors.note: Site signposting rule, not a retrieved claim
